question: Fitbit 的 awake 总时长为什么可能和 SleepLens 的 awake_min 不同？如果用睡眠日记核对，还应记录哪些时间和白天信息？

retrieved_evidence.title: Google Health ? Sleep Stage Estimates
retrieved_evidence.scope: Manufacturer-specific Fitbit/Pixel Watch information; not a universal device definition
retrieved_evidence.text: Google Health describes Fitbit and Pixel Watch sleep stages as estimates using wrist movement and heart-rate information, unlike laboratory sensors on the brain and muscles. Its light label likely includes N1 and N2; deep likely includes N3. This describes those products, not all wearables or SleepLens's synthetic records.

retrieved_evidence.title: NIH/NHLBI ? Insomnia Diagnosis
retrieved_evidence.scope: Clinical assessment and diary context; not self-diagnosis
retrieved_evidence.text: A sleep diary can record sleep and wake times, naps, daytime sleepiness, caffeine or alcohol use, and exercise. Clinical history also distinguishes going to bed, getting up, time taken to fall asleep, awakenings and time needed to return to sleep. Sleep onset and bedtime are different observations.

retrieved_evidence.title: NIH/NHLBI ? Insomnia Symptoms
retrieved_evidence.scope: Symptom context; no awakening-count diagnostic cutoff
retrieved_evidence.text: Frequent nighttime waking, difficulty staying asleep, or waking early without being able to return to sleep can occur with insomnia. Feeling unrefreshed, daytime sleepiness and difficulty concentrating also matter. An awakening count alone does not establish a diagnosis; this page gives no universal normal-count cutoff.

retrieved_evidence.title: Google Health ? Sleep Stage Estimates
retrieved_evidence.scope: Manufacturer-specific Fitbit/Pixel Watch information; not a universal device definition
retrieved_evidence.text: Google Health's awake total can include time before initial sleep, intermediate wakefulness and time after final awakening. SleepLens's awake_min includes only wakefulness between sleep onset and final awakening. These differently defined totals should not be directly equated.
